newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African govt says wants to save ERPM.
newsitem.headline: South African govt says wants to save ERPM.

text.p: The South African government said on Tuesday it wanted to save embattled East Rand Proprietary Mines Ltd which is under threat of closure.
ERPM managers Randgold and Exploration Company Ltd warned last month that the mine would have to close if present low bullion prices and lower-than-expected underground yields continued.

The Department of Minerals and Energy said in a statement on Tuesday that the government had been assisting ERP since 1990. It has granted the mine a series of loans totalling some 38 million rand of which the first loan of eight million rand was due for repayment this year.
"Due to the current low gold price and ERPM's present circumstances, consideration is being given to the rescheduling of the repayments," the statement said.
In terms of another agreement in December 1993, the government guaranteed loans totalling 252 million rand as part of its assistance package for ERPM.
"Government's intention is, therefore, to try to save the mine from closure," the statement said.
ERPM posted a 12.14 million rand net loss before capital expenditure in the three months to end-June 1997.
The mine produced 1,379 kg of gold in the June quarter.
